contract: template<unsigned BITS> struct RefCount { void acquire(); bool release(); };  starts at 1; acquire() is only called by a thread that already holds a reference; release() returns true exactly when the caller dropped the last reference and must destroy the object.
instantiate: template struct RefCount<3>; template struct RefCount<32>;
harness_note: the workers' writes to the object are plain ints, so the destroyer missing a happens-before edge is a data race
statement: Main and T worker threads share an object; each worker writes its part while holding a reference, may clone and drop extra references, then releases. Exactly one release reports 'last'; that release sees every write made before any release; nobody touches the object after it is freed; no data race; every operation returns.
scenario_rule: at least one scenario with reference cloning (K >= 1) and one with three workers
liveness_note: non-blocking contract; GenMC's spin-loop liveness heuristic misreports CAS retry loops, so termination is checked instead
